mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 7% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for four consecutive months is associated with reduced consumer confidence and spending power, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) and personal savings rate (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a shift from saving to investment, which typically boosts consumer and business confidence and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held constant at or below 0.5% for more than six months in a low-inflation environment (CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%) signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS <= 0.5% for >6 months AND CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 in two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 100000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 3% combined with a decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a strong demand environment, which typically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change > 3% AND UNRATE < 5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
